abstract: We report an experiment to demonstrate a quantum permutation determining algorithm with linear optical system. By employing photon polarization and spatial modes, we realize the quantum ququart states and all the essential permutation transformations. Compared with the classical case, this work determines the parity of the permutation in only one step of evaluation and displays the remarkable speedup of quantum algorithm. This experiment is accomplished in single photon level and exhibits strong universality in quantum computation.

specification.problem: Given black-box access to one of the 2d 'cyclic-type' permutations of d=4 elements (the d cyclic shifts and the d reflections forming the dihedral group D_4 acting on Z_4), decide with a single evaluation of the permutation which of the two classes it belongs to (the class the algorithm literature labels 'even'/positive-cyclic vs 'odd'/negative-cyclic), using a single ququart realized by photon polarization and spatial modes.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Reconstruct the single-qudit permutation-parity algorithm (Gedik-type) for d=4: one ququart register, Fourier-basis input state, permutation unitary from the 8-element dihedral set, inverse Fourier transform, computational-basis measurement. Explicit instance: d=4, omega=i, test permutations sigma(k)=k+1 mod 4 (shift) and sigma(k)=-k mod 4 (reflection). Outside scope: the linear-optical decomposition of the ququart gates into wave plates/beam splitters, single-photon source and detection details, measured fidelities, and the 'universality' claim of the abstract.

symbols.meaning: qudit dimension; d=4 for the ququart
primitive d-th root of unity, \omega = e^{2\pi i/d} = i for d=4
permutation of Z_4 given as a black box
permutation unitary acting on the ququart
quantum Fourier transform on one ququart
j-th Fourier-basis state of the ququart
symbols.domain: unit vector in C^4, j in Z_4

symbols.meaning: spatial-mode bit and polarization bit (H=0,V=1) encoding the ququart

equations.label: Ququart encoding in polarization and spatial modes
equations.description: The four-level photonic state is formed from two spatial modes and two polarizations; integer label k uses spatial bit as most significant bit.
equations.justification: The abstract states polarization and spatial modes realize ququart states; the specific bit ordering is a chosen convention.
assumptions: Spatial bit is the most significant bit; H maps to p=0, V to p=1.

equations.label: Fourier basis and QFT on the ququart
equations.description: Definition of the single-qudit QFT and its basis states; the algorithm's input is |\psi_1\rangle = F|1\rangle.
equations.justification: Standard single-qudit Fourier transform used in the Gedik-type permutation algorithm.

equations.label: Permutation unitaries (dihedral set)
equations.latex: U_\sigma|k\rangle = |\sigma(k)\rangle,\quad \sigma^{+}_m(k) = k + m \bmod d,\quad \sigma^{-}_m(k) = m - k \bmod d,\quad m \in Z_d
equations.description: The 2d permutations considered: d cyclic shifts (class '+', labelled even/positive in the algorithm) and d reflections (class '-', labelled odd/negative). Addition is modular.
equations.abstract_quote: we realize the quantum ququart states and all the essential permutation transformations
equations.justification: The single-qudit permutation-parity algorithm is defined on this dihedral family; the abstract's 'essential permutation transformations' is interpreted as this set.
assumptions: The experiment's permutation set is the 8-element dihedral family rather than all 24 elements of S_4; for d=4 the shift/reflection class does not coincide with S_4 sign parity, so 'parity' is understood in the algorithm's sense.

equations.label: Action of permutations on the Fourier input state
equations.description: Shifts leave |\psi_1\rangle invariant up to a global phase; reflections map it to |\psi_{d-1}\rangle up to a global phase (exact equalities).
equations.justification: Follows by substituting j = sigma(k) in eq_2 and eq_3: sum_k omega^k |k+m> = omega^{-m} sum_j omega^j |j>, and sum_k omega^k |m-k> = omega^m sum_j omega^{-j}|j>.

equations.label: Readout after inverse QFT
equations.description: A single computational-basis measurement deterministically yields 1 for the shift class and 3 for the reflection class; one evaluation of U_sigma suffices, versus two evaluations classically.
equations.abstract_quote: this work determines the parity of the permutation in only one step of evaluation
equations.justification: Combines eq_2 and eq_4 with F^dagger|psi_j> = |j>; the one-query claim is explicit in the abstract, the deterministic outcome mapping is inferred from the standard algorithm.
assumptions: Ideal (noiseless) gates and perfect single-photon detection.

registers.name: q
registers.size: 1 ququart (d=4), equivalently 2 qubits (spatial bit, polarization bit)
registers.role: Carries the Fourier-basis probe state and is acted on by the permutation unitary

specification.initial_state: |1\rangle = |s=0\rangle|p=1\rangle (then transformed by F to |\psi_1\rangle); equivalently prepare |\psi_1\rangle = \frac{1}{2}(|0\rangle + i|1\rangle - |2\rangle - i|3\rangle) directly.

steps.description: Prepare the ququart in |1\rangle and apply the QFT F to obtain the Fourier state |\psi_1\rangle.
Apply the black-box permutation unitary U_\sigma once (instance: sigma^+_1 shift or sigma^-_0 reflection).
Apply the inverse QFT F^\dagger to map the resulting Fourier state back to a computational-basis state.

specification.measurement: Measure the ququart in the computational basis (spatial mode and polarization of the single photon). Ideal outcome: k=1 for shift-class ('even') permutations, k=3 for reflection-class ('odd') permutations, each with probability 1.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map outcome 1 -> shift class ('even'), outcome 3 -> reflection class ('odd'); outcomes 0 or 2 indicate experimental error. Experimentally, repeat over many photons to estimate outcome probabilities / success rate.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the smallest useful instance chosen is d=4 with the 8 dihedral permutations, as this matches the ququart in the abstract and the Gedik-type algorithm.
The experiment implements the single-qudit Fourier-probe algorithm; the abstract does not spell out the algorithm's equations.
Bit ordering k = 2s + p and the H/V polarization labelling are conventions chosen here.
The 'parity' in the abstract is taken to mean the shift-vs-reflection class of the dihedral permutations, which for d=4 differs from S_4 sign parity.
